title: Zhongshan
capsule: Zhongshan (中山) was a non-Zhou state in the central Hebei plain, founded by the Beidi (White Di) peoples and occupying roughly the territory of the earlier Xianyu state, wedged between the larger Warring States of Zhao, Wei, and Yan. After Wei conquered it around 407 BCE, King Cuo restored independence by 381 BCE; in 323 BCE Zhongshan joined a five-state alliance and its ruler claimed the title wang (king), provoking jealousy from Qi. Zhao under King Wuling conducted systematic campaigns of dismemberment, completing the conquest around 296 BCE. Royal tomb excavations at Pingshan County in 1974–1978 yielded extraordinary bronze vessels with inscribed historical accounts, iron-armored cavalry equipment, and architectural plans, documenting a sophisticated hybrid steppe-Zhou court culture.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory around Lingshou is confirmed by the Pingshan archaeological excavations and inscribed texts; outer boundaries at different periods of the state's oscillating independence are reconstructed from transmitted texts rather than physical evidence.
